title: Advisory semantic anchor (not directly enforced): read and author a train as one linear end-to-end journey ending in one terminal contract

facts.note: Alternative signal (not a mandatory gate): a new observer must detect that the planner role/phase is authoring plans or decomposing a domain.

Alternative signal: a train specification artifact is read, created or edited. None of the supplied inputs shows a reliable way to identify train artifacts today. A new observer is needed that classifies an artifact as a train, either by an agreed plan-tree path/file-kind convention or by schema inspection (for example, an artifact declaring wagons/steps and a terminal contract).

Alternative signal: the read/create/edit operation is observable now. Linking it to a train artifact relies on the file_kind observer above. Read-only interpretation or classification counts; editing is not required.
Alternative signal only, never a mandatory lexical gate: the task text mentions trains or journeys.

values: deciding what a train is: interpreting, classifying, defining or reshaping a journey (steps, wagons, initial input, terminal contract)
facts.note: Alternative signal: judging whether the planner is deciding or relying on which journey a train names is not deterministically observable and needs LLM judgement. No edit or shape change is required.

fires: Planner drafts a new train for an end-to-end user/system journey across wagons.
Planner restructures an existing train's steps, participants, initial input or terminal step.
Planner decides whether a set of wagons forms one train or several.
Planner interprets or classifies an existing journey as a train (or not) without editing any train file.
doesNotFire: Coder implements how a train journey runs or whether it holds runtime state.
Tester writes runtime tests for a train's execution.
Planner edits a single wagon's internals without defining, interpreting or relying on any train's meaning.

given: a planner is decomposing a domain into trains, or interpreting/classifying an existing journey as a train
when: they define, reshape or classify a train
then: Use this advisory definition. It enforces nothing directly; the constraint/rule nodes that require it do the enforcing. A train names exactly one executable end-to-end journey: a strictly linear, ordered sequence of steps across declared wagons, from a declared initial input to exactly one terminal contract.
prefer: A full journey the domain can run end to end, not a fragment.
Strictly sequential steps between declared participants, with one coherent outcome, at least 2 wagons and ideally 3-7.
Declare the initial input and the artifacts moved from step to step.
Have the terminal step declare exactly one primary artifact, and derive the train's family from it.
avoid: Loops, routes or branching inside a train.
Bundling several journeys or outcomes into one train.
Multiple terminal contracts, or a family that disagrees with the terminal contract.
Specifying how the journey runs or what runtime state it holds; those are coder/tester concerns.
Treating this anchor as a separately enforced rule. Findings come from the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
why: A train names WHAT journey the domain must support. This anchor gives that a stable meaning, and the enforceable nodes that require it (linearity, scope, terminal contract, family) do the checking.
evidence: This node is advisory and not bound to a validator. Compliance is established through the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require this anchor: planner.train.linearity, planner.train.scope, planner.train.sequence, planner.train.participants, planner.train.initial-cargo-inputs-declared, planner.train.artifact-flow, planner.train.terminal-contract, planner.train.family, planner.train.family-matches-terminal-contract.
A reviewer confirms the train reads as one coherent end-to-end journey from a declared input to one terminal artifact.
verifier_detail: Advisory semantic anchor: a definitional node that gives the artifact a stable meaning. It is not itself bound to a validator and enforces nothing directly; the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require it protect it transitively.
Definition: train -> {executable, linear, single-outcome, wagon-composed, initial-input, single-terminal-contract}.
executable: an end-to-end journey the domain can run, not a fragment.
linear: strictly sequential steps, no loops/routes/branching (planner.train.linearity).
single-outcome: tells ONE coherent journey, 2 wagons minimum, 3-7 sweet spot (planner.train.scope).
wagon-composed: ordered sequence of steps between declared participants (planner.train.sequence, planner.train.participants).
initial-input: starts from a declared initial input and moves artifacts along (planner.train.initial-cargo-inputs-declared, planner.train.artifact-flow).

single-terminal-contract: terminal step declares exactly one primary artifact, the source of truth for family (planner.train.terminal-contract, planner.train.family, planner.train.family-matches-terminal-contract).
